lines.japanese: 渡来さんの家に来るのはこれで二回目だ。前に書いてもらった地図を思いだして、学校からまっすぐ向かってきた。
lines.english: This was my second visit to Watarai's home. I remembered the map she had drawn me and came straight from school.

lines.japanese: ああ、お菓子やジュースでも持ってくればよかったかな。でも財布も持ってないし仕方ないな。
lines.english: Oh, maybe I should've brought some snacks or juice. But I don't even have my wallet, so I guess there's nothing I can do.

lines.japanese: エレベーターで上がって目的の階に着くと、渡来さんの家はもうそこだ。
lines.english: Once the elevator reached the right floor, Watarai's apartment was right there.

lines.japanese: 僕は銀色の柱に映る自分を見て、髪型を整えてから、インターホンを押してみた。
lines.english: I checked myself in the silver pillar, fixed my hair, and pressed the intercom.

lines.japanese: 「どうぞー」
lines.english: “Come in.”

lines.japanese: 鉄製の扉がゆっくりと開き、渡来さんの部屋に僕は四日ぶりに足を踏みいれた。
lines.english: The iron door swung slowly open, and I stepped into Watarai's apartment for the first time in four days.

lines.japanese: 僕は渡来さんが開けてくれた扉を受けとめて、ゆっくりとドアを閉じた。
lines.english: I caught the door Watarai held open and closed it gently behind me.

lines.japanese: 「体は平気？」
lines.english: “Are you all right?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、大丈夫だよ。ちょっと痛むけど、このくらいなら動けるよ」
lines.english: “Mm-hm. I’m fine. It hurts a little, but not enough to stop me moving around.”

lines.japanese: 「無理したら駄目だよ。針生先輩、アフリカのなんとかって格闘技やってて、キック凄いんだから」
lines.english: “Don't push yourself. Hariu practices some African martial art or other, and his kicks are brutal.”

lines.japanese: 「……どうなるかと思った」
lines.english: “...I was scared of what might happen.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは、子供を叱るような、でもどこか安心したような声で僕に注意した。
lines.english: Watarai warned me in a voice like she was scolding a child, though she sounded relieved too.

lines.japanese: 「や、やだな。そんな、大げさだよ。平気、平気」
lines.english: “D-don't be silly. You're making too much of it. I'm fine. Really.”

lines.japanese: 「そっか。やっぱり男の子だ」
lines.english: “I see. You really are a boy.”

lines.japanese: 「あはは」
lines.english: “Ahaha.”

lines.japanese: この三日間、渡来さんには毎朝会ったし、そのたびに笑顔を見た気がするけど、見るたびに可愛さが増している気がする。
lines.english: I had seen Watarai every morning for the past three days, and I thought she had smiled each time. Yet somehow she seemed prettier every time I looked.

lines.japanese: 僕は照れくさくて直視できなくなったから、自分の足元に目線を移した。靴下の親指が少し擦りきれていて恥ずかしかった。
lines.english: I grew too embarrassed to look at her, so I lowered my eyes to my feet. The big toe of one sock had worn a little thin. That was embarrassing too.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、座って」
lines.english: “Well, sit down.”

lines.japanese: 「うんじゃあ座らせてもらうね……」
lines.english: Mm-hm. Okay, I'll sit down...

lines.japanese: 「あれっ？」
lines.english: “Wait.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんの部屋に入って感じたこと。なんだろう、どこか前と違う気がする。
lines.english: What I felt when I entered Watarai's room... what was it? Something seemed different from last time.

lines.japanese: 部屋の中は整ってるんだけど、なんていうか、こう……。
lines.english: The room was tidy, but somehow...

lines.japanese: 「はい、クッション」
lines.english: “Here. A cushion.”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう」
lines.english: “Thank you.”

lines.japanese: そうだ、前に来たときは、綺麗過ぎるくらい整頓してあったんだけど、今日は例えばキッチン……。
lines.english: Oh, right. Last time I came, it was almost too tidy. But today, for example, the kitchen...

lines.japanese: 部屋に来る途中で見かけた台所は、お皿やコップなどの食器類が流し台からはみ出るくらい重なっていた。
lines.english: The kitchen I'd passed on the way in had plates, glasses, and other dishes piled up until they spilled out of the sink.

lines.japanese: 「渡来さん、もしかして台所の蛇口が壊れて……」
lines.english: “Watarai, did your kitchen faucet break, or...?”

lines.japanese: 「話、いいかな」
lines.english: “Can we talk?”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは僕の言葉を遮るように、鋭い声で割りこんできた。
lines.english: Her sharp voice cut across mine.

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうだね。じゃあ渡来さんの話が終わってからおれの話もするよ」
lines.english: “Oh, right. Once you've finished, there's something I want to tell you too.”

lines.japanese: 僕はクッションを床におくと、片膝を立ててその上に座った。
lines.english: I set the cushion on the floor and sat on it with one knee raised.

lines.japanese: 「えーと」
lines.english: “Let's see...”

lines.japanese: 「さて、話すことは決まってたものの、何から始めればいいのかな」
lines.english: “Well. I know what I need to tell you, but where am I supposed to begin?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そんな、渡来さんの好きなように、ゆっくり話してくれればいいよ」
lines.english: Oh, no, just... tell me however you want. Take your time.

lines.japanese: 「うん、ありがとだ」
lines.english: “Mm. Much obliged.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんがスカートの裾を押さえながら、足の位置を動かす。その場所を見ないように頑張ったけど、眼球の周りの筋肉が悲鳴をあげているのが分かった。
lines.english: Holding down the hem of her skirt, Watarai shifted her legs. I fought not to look. The muscles around my eyes were soon screaming from the effort.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ好きなように話すけどいいよね」
lines.english: “Then I'll tell it however I like. That's all right with you?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、好きなように」
lines.english: “Mm-hm. However you like.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、まずは何から始めようかな」
lines.english: “Hmm. Where shall I begin?”

lines.japanese: 「だって、ねえ？　ひとに紹介するのなんて初めてだもんね」
lines.english: “I mean... I’ve never made introductions before, have I?”

lines.japanese: 「え？　なんのこと？」
lines.english: “Huh? What do you mean?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、じゃあ昔話から始めればいいよね」
lines.english: “All right. I’ll start at the beginning, then.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あれ？　渡来さん？　あの、誰と話してるの」
lines.english: “W-wait, Watarai. Um... who are you talking to?”

lines.japanese: 「私ね、小さい頃から友達って居なかったんだ」
lines.english: “You see, I never had any friends when I was little.”

lines.japanese: 「小さい頃……から？　え、だって、友達なら沢山いるじゃない」
lines.english: “Ever since you were little...? But you have lots of friends.”

lines.japanese: 「あはは、羽田君は分かってるくせに。知り合いなら沢山いるけど、友達なんて居ないよね。ねー、このひと面白いこと言うよね」
lines.english: Ahaha. You know better than that, Haneda. I know plenty of people, but I don't have any friends. See? This guy says the funniest things, doesn't he?

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは僕の顔を見たまま声をかけてくる。それは普通のことなんだけど……。
lines.english: Watarai spoke to me while looking me right in the face. That was perfectly normal, but...

lines.japanese: 「ひとと話すのは嫌いだったけど、やっぱり一人は寂しいし、とにかく友達が欲しかったんだ」
lines.english: I hated talking to people, but being alone got lonely, and I just really wanted a friend.

lines.japanese: 「うちは片親だから、家に帰ったら誰も居なかったんだよね。別に母親と仲は悪くないけど、普段家にいないから、一緒に遊ぶ友達が欲しかったの」
lines.english: “It was just my mother and me, so no one was there when I got home. It wasn't that we got along badly; she simply wasn't home much. I wanted a friend to play with.”

lines.japanese: 「でも、誰と話しても楽しくないし、逆にどんどんみんなとの距離が開いてばっかりなんだよね。だって、誰と話しても本当に言いたいことは口に出せないし、なのにみんなは寄ってくるじゃない？」
lines.english: But talking to anyone was no fun, and I just got farther and farther away from everyone instead. I mean, no matter who I talked to, I couldn't say what I really wanted to say. And yet everybody kept coming up to me, right?

lines.japanese: 「ああ、こんなんでいいんだって思うよね。私はつまらないのに、みんなは楽しそうにしてて、誰か気づくかなーって笑顔を増やせば増やすほど、喜んじゃうんだよ」
lines.english: “You start thinking, Oh, so this is all it takes. I'm bored to death, but everyone else looks delighted. You smile more and more, wondering if anyone will notice, and all it does is make them happier.”

lines.japanese: 「だったら、そんなの楽しくないし、もういいやって思うよね。かくして私は部屋に閉じこもりっきりの寂しい子になっちゃったわけだ」
lines.english: “Eventually you think, This isn't fun, so forget it. And thus I became a lonely little girl who shut herself in her room.”

lines.japanese: 「え、みんなの方から声をかけてくれるなんていいことじゃない」
lines.english: “But isn't it a good thing when other people talk to you first?”

lines.japanese: 「おれなんて、あんまり友達もいないしさ、うらやましいくらいかな、はは……」
lines.english: I don't have many friends myself, so I'm almost jealous, I guess. Ha ha...

lines.japanese: 「そっかなー、私ね、羽田君なら分かってくれると思うんだよね」
lines.english: “Do you? I think you, of all people, would understand.”

lines.japanese: 「興味ない話を延々するのって疲れるんだよ。でもそれはみんなが悪いんじゃなくて、私がずれてるんだ。でもやっぱり相手に合わせるのはしんどくてさ」
lines.english: “Going on and on about things you don't care about is exhausting. It's not their fault—I'm the one who's out of step. But it's still hard trying to fit in with them.”

lines.japanese: 「だから羽田君と話したときに、ついぽろっと言っちゃったんだと思うな。私は基本的に人間嫌いだからって」
lines.english: “I suppose that’s why it slipped out when I talked to you—that basically, I hate people.”

lines.japanese: 「続けるね」
lines.english: “I'll go on.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんが足を組みかえたけど、今度はあまり気にならなかった。それよりも、いま彼女はとても大切な話をしてる気がする。
lines.english: Watarai crossed her legs the other way, but this time I barely noticed. More importantly, I felt like she was telling me something really important.

lines.japanese: 「それでまあ、渡来さん家の一人娘は、ひと付きあいの苦手な引きこもりの子どもになっちゃいました」
lines.english: And so, well, the Watarai family's only daughter turned into a shut-in kid who was terrible with people.

lines.japanese: 「ってだけなら一人になってよかったね、楽だね、呼吸もしやすいねってことでよかったんだけど、やっぱり友達は欲しくなるものなんだよね」
lines.english: “If that had been the whole story, it would have ended happily enough. Good for her: she was alone, life was easy, she could breathe again. But sooner or later, you find yourself wanting a friend after all.”

lines.japanese: 「どんなひとならいいのかなー、んー、女の子はもういいかなー、でも、年上の男の子だと気を使うしなー。もし年下の話が合う男の子がいたら楽だろうな、って思ったわけ」
lines.english: “What kind of person would be good? Hmm... Maybe I'm done with girls? But older boys make me nervous. I thought it'd be easy if there were a younger boy I clicked with.”

lines.japanese: 「名前はお互い呼びやすいように、近い名前がいいなとか、男の子はロボットなんか好きなんじゃないかなとか、話のテンポはこのくらいが話しやすいなーとか」
lines.english: Like, maybe our names should sound similar so they'd be easy for us to say, or boys probably liked robots, or this kind of pace was easiest to talk at... stuff like that.

lines.japanese: 「そのときは理想の友達を考えるのが楽しくって、他のこととかどうでもよくなっちゃったんだよね。だって楽しいんだもん。ね、楽しいもんね。他から一切干渉されない私だけの世界」
lines.english: Back then, thinking up my perfect friend was so much fun that I stopped caring about anything else. Because it was fun. Right? It was fun, wasn't it? A world that was mine alone, where nobody else could interfere.

lines.japanese: 「そうやって、呼びやすい名前とか、顔とか性格とか考えてるうちに、ふと話しかけたくなっちゃったんだよね。あれ？　このひともしかして、いるんじゃない？って」
lines.english: While I was thinking up an easy name, and a face, and a personality, I suddenly felt like talking to him. Like, wait... maybe this person is actually here?

lines.japanese: 「で、その結果が」
lines.english: “And the result was...”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは立ちあがってガラッとクローゼットを開くと、その中から箱のような収納ケースを取りだした。
lines.english: Watarai stood, rattled open the closet, and took out a boxlike storage case.

lines.japanese: 「これ」
lines.english: “This.”

lines.japanese: 僕は中を覗いてみた。そこには、どこかで見たことがあるような、男の子用のおもちゃや、子ども服が詰まっている。
lines.english: I peered inside. It was packed with boys' toys and children's clothes that looked somehow familiar.

lines.japanese: 「え……これ、渡来さん、の……？」
lines.english: “Are these... yours, Watarai...?”

lines.japanese: 「あはは、違う、違う。そんなのじゃないんだ。あー、専門用語で言うならイマジナリー・コンパニオンってやつ」
lines.english: Ahaha, no, no. It's not like that. Um, if you want the technical term, it's what they call an imaginary companion.

lines.japanese: 「誰かに紹介するのは初めてなんだけどね。私の見えない友達」
lines.english: “I've never introduced him to anyone before. My invisible friend.”

lines.japanese: 「明日夢くん」
lines.english: “Asumu.”

lines.japanese: 「あすむくん？」
lines.english: “Asumu?”

lines.japanese: それはどこか遠くを見るわけでもなく、かと言ってこの部屋のどこかを見るでもなく、渡来さんは僕の顔を見ながら微笑んだ。
lines.english: Watarai smiled at me, her eyes neither looking into the distance nor at anything else in the room.

lines.japanese: 「も、ほんと楽しいんだよ。楽しいっていうより、楽？　疲れないっていうか、私の言いたいことだけ言ってもうんうんってうなずいてくれるんだもん」
lines.english: It's really fun. Or, not fun exactly—easy? Like, it doesn't wear me out. I can say nothing but what I want to say, and he'll still nod and go, ‘Uh-huh, uh-huh.’

lines.japanese: 「そんな子が側に居たら、他の子と遊ぼうなんて思わなくなっちゃうよね。だって楽しかったもん。他のひとには見えないとか話せないとかどうでもよくない？　だって私からすれば、すぐそこに居るんだよ」
lines.english: “With a boy like that beside you, why would you ever want to play with other children? It was fun. Who cared that no one else could see him or talk to him? As far as I was concerned, he was standing right there.”

lines.japanese: 「それは……えっと、どんな話をするのかな」
lines.english: “What do you... um. What sort of things do you talk about?”

lines.japanese: 「ほんとに普通の話だよね。クラスのあの子はどうとか、給食がおいしくなかったとか、あとあいつムカつく、今日楽しかった、なんか無性に寂しいとかだったっけ」
lines.english: Just really normal stuff, you know? Like what some kid in class did, or how lunch wasn't good, or that guy pisses me off, or today was fun, or I felt lonely for no reason... I think.

lines.japanese: 「あー、あと、格闘ごっことかよくやったよね。私がヒーローで、明日夢は怪獣。じょわっ！　いっつも私が苦戦するんだけど、最後には勝たせてくれたよね」
lines.english: “Oh, and we used to play-fight all the time, didn’t we? I was the hero, Asumu the monster. Hyah! I always had to fight hard, but you let me win in the end.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんがちらりと見た収納ケースの中には、ロボットや怪獣のおもちゃがいくつもあった。
lines.english: In the storage case Watarai glanced toward were several robot and monster toys.

lines.japanese: 「楽しかったよね」
lines.english: “We had fun, didn't we?”

lines.japanese: 「羽田君もそういうのないかな。あー、楽だなー、楽っていうか、一人になりたいときは、何も言わなくても居なくなってくれるし、話したいときは気がついたら側に居るし」
lines.english: Didn't you ever have anything like that, Haneda? Like, ahh, this is easy... or, not easy exactly. If I wanted to be alone, he'd disappear without me saying anything, and when I wanted to talk, I'd realize he was right beside me.

lines.japanese: 「いま思いだすと、結構酷いことも言ってたかな。あっちいけーとか、いまはひとりがいいーとか。でも、ほんとに寂しいときは側に居てくれたし、その違いを分かってくれる子だったんだ」
lines.english: Looking back, I guess I said some pretty awful things too. Like, ‘Go awayyy,’ or ‘I wanna be alone right nowww.’ But when I was really lonely, he stayed with me. He was someone who understood the difference.

lines.japanese: 「ん……んん？　あの、でも、その子は実際には居ないんだよね？」
lines.english: “Mm... Hmm? But that boy doesn’t actually exist, does he?”

lines.japanese: 「いるよ。うん、居たの。少なくとも私は居たって思ってる」
lines.english: “He does. Or—he did. At least, I believe he was there.”

lines.japanese: 「それは……」
どうなんだろう。渡来さんの中にいる、渡来さんだけの、渡来さんのための友達。
lines.english: What was I to make of it? A friend inside Watarai, belonging only to Watarai, made for Watarai alone.

lines.japanese: そんな都合のいい存在が、この世にいるんだろうか。
lines.english: Did anything that convenient really exist?

lines.japanese: 「……居たんだね」
lines.english: “...He was there.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、居たよ」
lines.english: “Yes. He was.”

lines.japanese: そう、それはいまここで話すべきことじゃない。渡来さんが居たって言うなら、それは事実だと認めるしかないんだ。
lines.english: Right. That wasn't what I should be questioning here. If Watarai said he was there, then I had to accept that he was.

lines.japanese: 「でも、いまは会えないんだ」
lines.english: “But you can't see him now.”

lines.japanese: 「分かっちゃった？」
lines.english: “You figured it out?”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは、笑顔のままだったけど、どこか寂しそうに、顔を傾けながら収納ケースを部屋の隅に押しやった。
lines.english: Watarai was still smiling, but she looked a little lonely as she tilted her head and pushed the storage case into the corner.

lines.japanese: 「私みたいなケースの子供って、広い目で見ればそう珍しいものじゃないんだって」
lines.english: “Apparently children like me aren’t all that unusual, if you take a broad enough view.”

lines.japanese: 「よくいる想像力の豊かな子。でもみんな成長して大人へ近づくにつれて、空想が空想でしかないんだって悟って、自然と会わなくなるんだって」
lines.english: They're just normal kids with big imaginations. But she said that as they grow up and get closer to being adults, they realize make-believe is only make-believe, and naturally stop seeing them.

lines.japanese: 「やっぱりね、学校には行くわけだし、色々と用事も出来てくると、部屋に居られる時間もなくなってくるもんね。一日、二日って時間が空くたびに、顔を合わせるのが辛くなっちゃったんだよね」
lines.english: You have to go to school, after all, and once you start having all kinds of things to do, you don't have as much time to stay in your room. Every time a day or two went by, it got harder to face him again.

lines.japanese: 「私がいつか、三日くらい空けちゃったのかな。どうしよう、なんて言おうと思って『久しぶり』って声をかけたの。多分、顔は笑えてたと思う。うん、笑ってた」
lines.english: “Once, I think I went three days without seeing him. What do I do? What do I say? I wondered. Then I said, ‘Long time no see.’ I think I managed to smile. Yes. I was smiling.”

lines.japanese: 「それからいつの間にかだったなあ……もう、会えなくなっちゃった」
lines.english: Then at some point after that... I couldn't see him anymore.

lines.japanese: 「でもいま……」
lines.english: “But just now...”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、会えなかった」
lines.english: “No. I couldn't see him.”

lines.japanese: 「そっか」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、ふりだけになっちゃった」
lines.english: “Mm-hm. Now all I can do is pretend.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんの手が柔らかく、きゅっと握られていた。きっとそのときのことを思いだしたんだと思う。
lines.english: Watarai gently closed her hand into a fist. She must have been remembering that moment.

lines.japanese: ちょっと寂しそうな顔をしてたけど、どこかすっきりしたような表情にも見えた。
lines.english: She looked a little lonely, yet somehow relieved too.

lines.japanese: 「でも、どうして急にこの話をしてくれようと思ったの？」
lines.english: “But why did you suddenly decide to tell me all this?”

lines.japanese: 「どうして？」
lines.english: “Why?”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんが驚いたように顔を上げた。
lines.english: Watarai raised her face in surprise.

lines.japanese: 「どうしてって、羽田君なら分かってくれると思ったからだよね」
lines.english: “Why? Because I thought you would understand, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ……そうだね、おれは分かる気がするよ」
lines.english: “Oh... Yes. I think I do understand.”

lines.japanese: 「何でも話せる相手っているといいよね。うん、それは楽しいと思う。おれにはなんでも話してよ」
lines.english: “It must be wonderful to have someone you can tell anything to. Mm-hm. It sounds like fun. You can tell me anything too.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃなくて」
lines.english: “That isn't what I mean.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは手を顔の前でぱたりと倒す。小さく首を横に振った。
lines.english: Watarai tipped her hand down in front of her face and gave a tiny shake of her head.

lines.japanese: 「うん話してて楽だってのもあるけど、羽田君は私と同じ」
lines.english: “Yes, you are easy to talk to. But what I mean is that you're the same as me.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「グレタガルド的なアレ」
lines.english: “That whole Gretagard thing.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんが微笑んだので、僕は微笑みかえしながら首を傾げた。
lines.english: Watarai smiled, so I smiled back and tilted my head.

lines.japanese: 彼女は急に何を言ってるんだろう。確かに夢みたいな世界の話はしたけど、グレタガルドは実際にあるって彼女は信じてくれたはず……。
lines.english: What was she talking about all of a sudden? Sure, I'd told her about a world that sounded like a dream, but she was supposed to believe Gretagard was real...

lines.japanese: 「嘘だよって言ってるんじゃなくて、羽田君の作った世界だってことを言ってるんだよ。私と同じ、都合のいい世界」
lines.english: “I'm not calling you a liar. I'm saying it's a world you created. A convenient world, just like mine.”

lines.japanese: 「そっちの世界に居れば、いつだって楽だと思うよ。でも、いつまでもそこには居られないよね」
lines.english: “I'm sure everything is easy while you're in that world. But you can't stay there forever, can you?”

lines.japanese: 「いや渡来さん、グレタガルドは本当の話なんだ」
lines.english: “No, Watarai. Gretagard is real.”

lines.japanese: 「よし分かった、これ見て」
lines.english: “All right. I understand. Look at this.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんはテレビの下から一昔前のゲーム機を出して、そのスイッチをｏｎにした。
lines.english: Watarai pulled an old game console out from beneath the television and switched it on.

lines.japanese: ＲＯＭカセットのゲーム機は起動も早い。製作会社のロゴが映ったあと、すぐタイトル画面に移行した。
lines.english: Cartridge consoles started quickly. The developer's logo appeared, and almost at once the title screen followed.

lines.japanese: そのゲームのタイトルは「ウイングクエスト」。
lines.english: The game was titled Wing Quest.

lines.japanese: 今から１０年以上前に流行ったゲームだ。かなり人気があって、当時の子どもたちはみんな一度はやったはず……なんだけど、不思議と僕の記憶にはない。
lines.english: It had been a tremendous hit more than ten years ago. Practically every child at the time must have played it at least once... yet, strangely, I had no memory of it.

lines.japanese: 「はは……渡来さん、ＲＰＧなんてやるんだ。随分古いゲームをやるんだね」
lines.english: “Ha ha... I didn't know you played RPGs. This one's awfully old.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、ＲＰＧゲームなんて初めてやった」
lines.english: “Mm-hm. This is the first RPG game I've ever played.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は相変わらずロールプレイングゲームの呼び方を勘違いしていた。
lines.english: She still called role-playing games the wrong thing.

lines.japanese: そういえばふたりでゲームショップへ行ったとき、何かのＲＰＧを買っていた……
lines.english: Come to think of it, she had bought some kind of RPG when we visited the game shop together...

lines.japanese: 「ほんと初めてだからあんまり進んでないんだけど、いまね、ガルーダを助けたところなんだ」
lines.english: “It's really my first one, so I haven't gotten very far. I've just rescued Garuda.”

lines.japanese: 「ガルーダ？」
lines.english: “Garuda?”

lines.japanese: 「そう。なんて言ったかな、どこかの場所に閉じこめられてたから助けなきゃいけなくてさ」
lines.english: “Right. What was it again? He was trapped somewhere, so I had to save him.”

lines.japanese: 「イーグルとファルコンを助けたところのセーブデータもあるよ。見る？」
lines.english: “I have save files from just after rescuing Eagle and Falcon too. Want to see?”

lines.japanese: 彼女はリセットボタンを押して、データをロードしようとしていた。僕はその間に、カセットと一緒にあった説明書を手に取ってみた。
lines.english: She pressed reset and started loading another save. In the meantime, I picked up the instruction booklet beside the cartridge.

lines.japanese: １０年以上前の説明書は、小さくて薄っぺらかった。開いてすぐに、世界地図みたいな背景の上にゲームの説明がある。
lines.english: The decade-old booklet was small and flimsy. Immediately inside, the game's premise was printed over a background resembling a map of the world.

lines.japanese: ――まだ人がふしぎな生き物たちと暮らしていたころの話。一人の王が国を作り、グレタガルドと名づけました。
lines.english: —This is a tale from an age when humankind still lived beside creatures of wonder. A king founded a realm and named it Gretagard.

lines.japanese: 平和な日が長くつづいていましたが、ある日、つばさの生えた“翼人”たちに国が襲われ、グレタガルドはほろんでしまいました。
lines.english: Long years of peace followed. Then one day, winged beings known as the Wingmen attacked. Gretagard was destroyed.

lines.japanese: その時、王のために命をとして戦った聖騎士ホークはとらえられ、３人のなかまたちとともに奈落（アビス）のおく深くに封印されてしまったのです。
lines.english: The holy knight Hawk, who staked his life in battle for the king, was captured and sealed with his three companions in the uttermost depths of the Abyss.

lines.japanese: からくも危機をだっしたプリンセス・ダヴは、聖騎士ホークを召喚することに成功しました。
lines.english: Princess Dove, who narrowly escaped the disaster, succeeded in summoning the holy knight Hawk.

lines.japanese: 「もはやグレタガルドを救えるのはあなたしかいません。他の仲間たちをさがし出し、ツヴァイ城塞を取りもどすのです」
lines.english: ‘You alone can save Gretagard now. Seek out your companions and reclaim Fortress Zwei.’

lines.japanese: あなたは聖騎士ホークとなり、イーグル、ファルコン、ガルーダの仲間を集めて、グレタガルドに平和を取り戻さなくてはなりません。あなたの冒険はいま始まったのです……。
lines.english: You must become the holy knight Hawk, gather your companions Eagle, Falcon, and Garuda, and restore peace to Gretagard. Now your adventure begins...

lines.japanese: 「はは、よく出来てるね……すごい偶然だな、おれの知ってるグレタガルドそっくりだ」
lines.english: Ha ha, it's really well made... What a coincidence. It looks just like the Gretagard I know.

lines.japanese: 「出来すぎだよね。ていうか、こんな偶然、ある・わけ・ないっ」
lines.english: “A little too exact, don't you think? I mean, there. Is. No. Way. this is a coincidence.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんがぴこぴこを置いて振りかえった。
lines.english: Watarai set down the beepy little controller and turned around.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君の理想の世界は、全部これのパクリっ！」
lines.english: “Your perfect world is a total rip-off of this game!”

lines.japanese: 「なにか理由があるんだよ……あ！　も、もしかして、このゲームの製作者が、おれみたいにグレタガルドの住人？　こんなことが出来るのは、科学者ギュンター？」
lines.english: “There must be some explanation... Ah! C-could the game's creator be an inhabitant of Gretagard, like me? Who else could do this? The scientist Günther?”

lines.japanese: 「まだ言ってるの」
lines.english: “You're still on about that?”

lines.japanese: 「お姫様裏技でねー、名前も変えられるんだよね。てことは、私をヒロインにしてくれたってことだよね。あはは、ちょっと照れちゃった」
lines.english: “There's a cheat that lets you change the princess's name too. So you made me the heroine, didn't you? Ahaha. I'm a little embarrassed.”

lines.japanese: 「あっ！　ご、ごめん……」
lines.english: “Oh! I-I'm sorry...”

lines.japanese: 「認めた」
lines.english: “You admitted it.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「虚構の、世界だって、いま、認めた」
lines.english: A fictional... world. You just... admitted it.

lines.japanese: 「ち、違うよ違う、おれは聖騎士ホーク……グレタガルドは、本当にあるんだ……」
lines.english: “N-no, you're wrong. I'm the holy knight Hawk... Gretagard is real...”

lines.japanese: それまでゲーム機に向かっていた渡来さんが、体ごと僕に向けて迫ってきた。
lines.english: Watarai, who until then had faced the console, turned her whole body toward me and closed in.

lines.japanese: 四つん這いの姿勢のまま、両手を前脚に見立てて近づいてくる様は、扇情的でもあり恐くもある。
lines.english: She approached on all fours, her hands serving as forelegs. The sight was seductive and frightening at once.

lines.japanese: 「ある、あるよ……グレタガルドは本当にある、あるんだよ……だって、あの世界では、おれのことをみんなが待っているから……」
lines.english: “It is. It is real... Gretagard truly exists. It has to... Because everyone in that world is waiting for me...”

lines.japanese: 「でないとおれのことを求めてくれるひとは……おれを必要としてくれる世界がなくなっちゃうんだ……だからグレタガルドは……」
lines.english: “Otherwise, there'd be no one who wanted me... no world that needed me... So Gretagard has to...”

lines.japanese: 「ないよ」
lines.english: “It doesn't.”

lines.japanese: 僕は止めを刺された。
lines.english: She dealt me the finishing blow.
